# `silk/core/result`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Completed outcomes that hold a success value or a failure value as ordinary data.

## When to use
Use [`Result`](#Result) when a caller must keep, return, or inspect an outcome as a value, and the
failure needs a reason. Use `silk.core.option.Option` when "no value" needs no reason. Use an
effect failure channel (`!`) when the failure must propagate with `fail` and `run`.

Use [`map`](#Result.impl.map) to transform a success, [`mapError`](#Result.impl.mapError) to transform a failure, [`flatMap`](#Result.impl.flatMap) to chain a
step that can also fail, and [`unwrapOr`](#Result.impl.unwrapOr) to get a plain value with a fallback.

## Details
`Result<A, F>` is a union with the variants [`Success`](#Result.Success) and [`Failure`](#Result.Failure). Each combinator
consumes the result. The selected value moves into the output. A value that the operation does
not use is dropped.

A `Result` is completed data. It does not run, it needs no provider, and it does not propagate.
`Effect.result` runs an effect and gives its outcome as a `Result`.

## Examples
### Chain two steps that can fail
```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }

fn half(value: i32) -> Result<i32, string<'static>> {
  if value % 2 != 0 {
    return Result<i32, string<'static>>.failResult("odd")
  }
  return Result<i32, string<'static>>.succeed(value / 2)
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let quarter = Result<i32, string<'static>>.succeed(80)
    |> Result<i32, string<'static>>.flatMap<i32>(half)
    |> Result<i32, string<'static>>.flatMap<i32>(half)
    |> Result<i32, string<'static>>.unwrapOr(-1)
  let failed = Result<i32, string<'static>>.succeed(6)
    |> Result<i32, string<'static>>.flatMap<i32>(half)
    |> Result<i32, string<'static>>.flatMap<i32>(half)
    |> Result<i32, string<'static>>.unwrapOr(-1)
  if quarter != 20 || failed != -1 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Result` with `import silk.core.result { Result }`.

<a id="Result"></a>

## `Result`

```silk
pub union Result<A, F>
```

A completed outcome that owns a success value of type `A` ([`Success`](#Result.Success)) or a failure value of
type `F` ([`Failure`](#Result.Failure)).

### When to use

Use `Result` as a return type when an operation can fail and the caller must handle the failure
as a value. `Effect.result` also gives the outcome of an effect as a `Result`.

### Details

Create values with [`succeed`](#Result.impl.succeed) and [`failResult`](#Result.impl.failResult). A `match` on `move result` consumes the
result. A `match` on a borrow keeps the result available.

### Examples

#### Handle both cases with `match`

```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.num.u8

fn parseDigit(byte: u8) -> Result<i32, u8> {
  if byte < 48 || byte > 57 {
    return Result<i32, u8>.failResult(byte)
  }
  return Result<i32, u8>.succeed(byte - 48 |> u8.toI32)
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let digit = match move parseDigit(55) {
    Result<i32, u8>.Success { value } => value
    Result<i32, u8>.Failure { error } => -1
  }
  if digit != 7 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

## Implementation `Result<A, F>`

```silk
impl<A, F> Result<A, F>
```

<a id="Result.impl.succeed"></a>

### Associated function `succeed`

```silk
pub fn succeed(value: A) -> Result<A, F>
```

Returns a successful `Result<A, F>` that owns `value`.

#### Details

Write both type arguments, as in `Result<i32, string<'static>>.succeed(1)`. No argument gives
the compiler the failure type `F`.

<a id="Result.impl.failResult"></a>

### Associated function `failResult`

```silk
pub fn failResult(error: F) -> Result<A, F>
```

Returns a failed `Result<A, F>` that owns `error`.

#### Details

Write both type arguments, as in `Result<i32, string<'static>>.failResult("empty")`. No
argument gives the compiler the success type `A`. The name is not `fail` because `fail` is a
keyword.

<a id="Result.impl.map"></a>

### Method `map`

```silk
pub fn map<B>(self: Self, transform: once fn(A) -> B) -> Result<B, F>
```

Returns `transform(value)` as a success if `self` is a success. Returns the same failure if
`self` is a failure.

#### When to use

Use `map` when the transform always succeeds. Use [`flatMap`](#Result.impl.flatMap) when the transform can also
fail. Use [`mapError`](#Result.impl.mapError) to change the failure value.

#### Details

`transform` runs one time for a success and does not run for a failure. This function
consumes `self`. It changes only the success type.

<a id="Result.impl.mapError"></a>

### Method `mapError`

```silk
pub fn mapError<G>(self: Self, transform: once fn(F) -> G) -> Result<A, G>
```

Returns `transform(error)` as a failure if `self` is a failure. Returns the same success if
`self` is a success.

#### When to use

Use `mapError` to convert a failure into the failure type of the caller, or to add context to
a failure. [`flatMap`](#Result.impl.flatMap) needs the same failure type in each step, so use `mapError` to align
the types first.

#### Details

`transform` runs one time for a failure and does not run for a success. This function consumes
`self`. It changes only the failure type.

<a id="Result.impl.flatMap"></a>

### Method `flatMap`

```silk
pub fn flatMap<B>(self: Self, transform: once fn(A) -> Result<B, F>) -> Result<B, F>
```

Returns the result that `transform` produces for a success. Returns the same failure if `self`
is a failure.

#### When to use

Use `flatMap` to chain steps where each step can fail. The output is one `Result<B, F>`, not a
nested `Result<Result<B, F>, F>`. Use [`map`](#Result.impl.map) when the step cannot fail.

#### Details

`transform` runs one time for a success and does not run for a failure. The first failure
stops the chain. This function consumes `self`.

#### Gotchas

`transform` must return the same failure type `F`. If the steps use different failure types,
convert them with [`mapError`](#Result.impl.mapError) first.

<a id="Result.impl.unwrapOr"></a>

### Method `unwrapOr`

```silk
pub fn unwrapOr(
    self: Self,
    /// The value to return if `self` is a failure. It is dropped if `self` is a success.
    fallback: A,
  ) -> A
```

Returns the success value. Returns `fallback` if `self` is a failure.

#### When to use

Use `unwrapOr` when one default value is correct for each failure. Use `match` when the
failure value controls the recovery or the caller must keep it.

#### Details

This function consumes `self` and `fallback`. It returns one value. It drops the failure value
or the unused fallback.

#### Gotchas

The failure value is dropped without a report. The caller evaluates `fallback` before the
call, also when `self` is a success.

<a id="Result.impl.unwrapOr.fallback"></a>

#### Parameter `fallback`

```silk
fallback: A
```

The value to return if `self` is a failure. It is dropped if `self` is a success.
